ov: The tailless primates of sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia: the gibbons, or lesser apes, and the great apes, which are the orangutans, gorillas, chimpanzees, bonobos and, scientifically, humans. The answers here are for the non-human apes; each species has its own page.

why.dg: Chimpanzees in particular can be dangerous, even to adult humans, when frightened or aggressive.

rg: Sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia; gibbons live only in Asia.
df: Mostly plants (fruit, leaves, stalks, roots, nuts and seeds), plus some animals.

cf.tip: Apes have no tail. Some tailless monkeys, such as the Barbary "ape", are called apes but are really monkeys.

fx: Every non-human ape species is threatened with extinction; all orangutans and gorillas are critically endangered.
Ebola has killed at least a third of all gorillas and chimpanzees since 1990.
